copyPanel.formula: Area = (Number of Sides) × (Area of One Triangle)
steps: 1. Decompose the regular polygon from center into n congruent triangles
2. Find the area of one triangle using A = ½ × side × apothem (height)
3. Multiply by the total number of sides

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Rooftop Garden
revealWordProblem.text: The firm is designing a regular decagon-shaped rooftop garden bed. It decomposes into 10 congruent triangles from the center, each with a base of 3 feet and a height of 4 feet. The garden center charges $5 per square foot for soil and plants. What is the total cost to fill the garden bed?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: One triangle: A = ½ × 3 × 4 = 6 sq ft. The decagon has 10 sides, so it has 10 triangles: 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft. Cost = 60 × $5 = $300.

questions.stem: A regular hexagon is divided into 6 equal triangles from the center. Each triangle has a base of 6 ft and a height of 5.2 ft. What is the area of one triangle? Use the given heights; nonsquare heights are rounded, so their areas are estimates.
questions.explanation: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 6 × 5.2 = 15.6 square feet.
choiceFeedback: 11.2 comes from adding 6 + 5.2. Area means multiply base × height, then take half.
The number is right, but ft measures length. Area needs square units (sq ft).
31.2 is 6 × 5.2 — the full rectangle. One triangle is half of that: multiply by ½.
hints: Focus on just ONE of the 6 triangles: its base is 6 ft and its height is 5.2 ft.
One triangle uses A = ½ × b × h — don't multiply by 6 yet; that step is for the whole hexagon.
Compute ½ × 6 × 5.2: take half of 6 first, then multiply by 5.2. Label it in sq ft.
questions.stemEs: Un hexágono regular se divide en 6 triángulos iguales desde el centro. Cada triángulo tiene una base de 6 ft y una altura de 5.2 ft. ¿Cuál es el área de un triángulo? Usa las alturas dadas; las de figuras que no son cuadrados están redondeadas, así que sus áreas son estimaciones.
questions.explanationEs: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 6 × 5.2 = 15.6 pies cuadrados.
hintsEs: Concéntrate en solo UNO de los 6 triángulos: su base es de 6 pies y su altura de 5.2 pies.
Un triángulo usa A = ½ × b × h; todavía no multipliques por 6, ese paso es para el hexágono completo.
Calcula ½ × 6 × 5.2: saca primero la mitad de 6 y luego multiplica por 5.2. Etiquétalo en pies².

choiceFeedback: That is the area of ONE of the congruent triangles. The hexagon is made of 6 of them — how many triangle areas do you still need to add?
That is 4 triangles, not 6. Re-count how many congruent triangles the hexagon breaks into.
You multiplied by 12 instead of 6. Count the congruent triangles the hexagon decomposes into before you multiply.
hints: Find one central triangle’s area: ½ × 6 × 5.2 = 15.6 sq ft using the rounded height.

reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Area of Regular Polygons is stopping after finding the area of ONE triangle and reporting that as the total area — or adding the number of triangles instead of multiplying. Remember: total area = (one triangle's area) × (number of sides), not (one triangle's area) + (number of sides).

level3.prompt: A regular hexagon and a regular pentagon are each divided into congruent central triangles. In both polygons, each central triangle has area 15 sq ft. Which polygon has greater total area? Explain why the triangle count matters. The two polygons have different side lengths.
level3.sentenceFrame: Each triangle has area ___. The hexagon has ___ triangles, so its area is ___. The pentagon has ___ triangles, so its area is ___. Therefore ___ .
level3.hint: Identify each shape; write area formula; add results.
hints: Each central triangle has the same AREA, but the triangles need not have the same shape.
A hexagon has 6 central triangles; a pentagon has 5.
Compare 6 × 15 with 5 × 15.
level3.explanation: The hexagon has area 6 × 15 = 90 sq ft. The pentagon has area 5 × 15 = 75 sq ft. The hexagon has 15 sq ft more because it has one additional triangle of that area. Equal triangle areas do not require equal bases and heights.
level3.explanationEs: El hexágono tiene área 6 × 15 = 90 pies². El pentágono tiene área 5 × 15 = 75 pies². El hexágono tiene 15 pies² más porque tiene un triángulo adicional de esa área. Tener áreas iguales no exige bases y alturas iguales.

level3.hint: Run the area formula backward: total area = number of triangles × ½ × base × height. Fill in what you know, then solve for the missing factor.
hints: Write the equation for the row before you compute anything: total = n × (½ × b × h).
Hexagon row: 6 × (½ × 9 × h) = 216 simplifies to 27h = 216, so divide.
The octagon row is different — the unknown is the triangle COUNT: n × (½ × 4 × 5) = 80 becomes 10n = 80.
level3.explanation: Use total = n × ½ × base × height. With rounded measurements: hexagon 216 = 27h gives h = 8 ft; octagon 80 = 10n gives n = 8; decagon 69 = 15h gives h = 4.6 ft. The square is exact: 144 = 4 × ½ × b × 6 = 12b, so b = 12 ft.
level3.explanationEs: Usa total = n × ½ × base × altura. Con medidas redondeadas: hexágono 216 = 27h da h = 8 pies; octágono 80 = 10n da n = 8; decágono 69 = 15h da h = 4.6 pies. El cuadrado es exacto: 144 = 4 × ½ × b × 6 = 12b, así que b = 12 pies.
hintsEs: Escribe la ecuación de la fila antes de calcular: total = n × (½ × b × h).
Fila del hexágono: 6 × (½ × 9 × h) = 216 se simplifica a 27h = 216, así que divide.
La fila del octágono es distinta: la incógnita es la CANTIDAD de triángulos. n × (½ × 4 × 5) = 80 se convierte en 10n = 80.
level3.stem: Use total area = number of triangles × ½ × base × height to find each missing value. Nonsquare measurements are rounded; use the displayed values.
level3.stemEs: Usa área total = cantidad de triángulos × ½ × base × altura para hallar cada valor que falta. Las medidas de figuras que no son cuadrados están redondeadas; usa los valores mostrados.
